paragraphs: The 630d joined the 6 Series range in 2015 as a Gran Coupe-only diesel addition, running until the 6 Series was discontinued in 2018. It uses the B57 — a 3.0-litre inline-six diesel that's part of BMW's newer B-series engine family, sharing its architecture with the widely-regarded B58 petrol unit. The B57 is generally considered a reliable engine, without any major widely-reported defect patterns. The 6 Series was discontinued entirely in 2018 and succeeded by the 8 Series, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: The 630d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the 630d was only offered for a relatively short production window (2015–2018) and exclusively as a Gran Coupe, engine compatibility is generally straightforward — all UK-market 630d models use the B57. However, we always confirm your exact vehicle specification via registration or VIN before any work begins, to ensure every component is correctly matched to your car's specific build.
